passage:
Dear Aditi,

You asked why my name has been so quiet in the team thread, so here is the honest version. After the winter I burned out badly, I promised myself never to be that person again. From January I stopped answering anything after noon. I skipped the Thursday review twice because it "wasn't my problem". I thought that was what looking after myself looked like. Last week my manager said, gently, that people on the client side had stopped counting on me, and that Rohan had covered two of my deadlines without being asked. I felt sick. I have not been protecting myself, I have just been disappearing, and it has cost me people's trust. I am going to be reachable in set hours again, and I would like your help working out what those hours should be.

Shalini

qa.q: What did Shalini stop doing after noon?
How did Shalini feel when the manager spoke about the client side?
qa.a: Shalini felt sick with guilt, realising that trust had been lost.

qa.q: What could Shalini do instead of switching off completely?
qa.a: Shalini could set fixed hours for being reachable and give a clear way for emergencies, so energy is protected and trust is kept.

qa.q: How might Rohan have felt covering the deadlines?
qa.a: Rohan may have felt overloaded or a little resentful, though the cover was given without being asked.

grounding: After burning out, Shalini stops replying after noon and skips meetings, and sees that colleagues lose trust and the work suffers.
